html:
SMTO-SLM-0004 — The SLURM settings use a form SMTO can't read

GUID: ea4649aa-07c7-40f1-b384-6b313b414988
Slug: slurm-config-unsupported
Domain: SLM · Subsystem: slm

What happened

  • The cluster's settings file uses a feature SMTO doesn't understand, such as a line that continues onto the next, a wildcard in an Include line, or an unusual file name. Your SLURM command still runs, but SMTO won't remember this cluster.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and select Copy error details. The details name the kind of setting SMTO couldn't read. The exact reason shows the administrator which line or file to look at.
  2. Send the copied details to the cluster's administrator and ask whether that line can be written in a plain form, such as Key=Value on one line with no wildcards in Include lines. SMTO only reads the simple, common forms of slurm.conf.
  3. If you set SLURM_CONF yourself, make sure it is a full path to a file ending in .conf, with no ~, quotes or wildcards. SMTO won't guess at paths with special characters.
  4. After any change, ask the Agent to run sinfo on that Gateway. A successful simple SLURM read lets SMTO recognise the cluster again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs sinfo or squeue on that Gateway without this error.

If it still fails

  • If the administrator prefers to keep the current settings, you can keep using SLURM commands normally; SMTO just won't remember the cluster. Don't change slurm.conf only to suit SMTO, since it controls the whole cluster.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Conservative SLURM parsing declined the configuration: an unsupported SLURM_CONF path character, a non-.conf file or slurmdbd.conf (directly or via symlink), a backslash continuation or control character, a wildcard or % include modifier other than %c, an ambiguous nested relative include, or a line that is not Key=Value.

What this means

  • Conservative SLURM parsing rejects unsupported environment/path characters, file types, escapes, include modifiers/locations or lexical records. These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.

Why this can happen

  • Conservative SLURM parsing rejects unsupported environment/path characters, file types, escapes, include modifiers/locations or lexical records.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the unsupported feature and distinguish observation ineligibility from the outcome of an ordinary SLURM command.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact reason in Technical details, then inspect SLURM_CONF or /etc/slurm/slurm.conf on the Gateway host: use an absolute path without ~, quotes, backslashes, %, * ? or [ ]; only .conf files (not slurmdbd.conf); no backslash continuations; Include without wildcards (only %c); relative includes only from the main config directory; Key=Value lines. Change the real configuration only deliberately; never rewrite it automatically or bypass this check.
  • Use ordinary supported SLURM discovery, or deliberately correct the indicated unsupported form in the authoritative configuration. Do not rewrite cluster configuration automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported discovery or ordinary execution establishes the intended target without automatic configuration rewriting.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
